title: The Passive with Ser: Tenses and Agreement

sections.content: You know the *ser* passive from B1 Unit 18: *La ley fue aprobada por el Parlamento*. It works because the thing that is affected becomes the subject, and the participle describes it, so the participle agrees with it like an adjective: *el puente fue construido*, *las casas fueron construidas*. What is new at B2 is the range. Only *ser* changes tense; the participle stays as it is. So you can use the passive for what happened (*fue publicada*), what has happened (*ha sido publicada*) and what will happen (*será publicada*).

sections.title: One participle, three tenses
rows: El puente ha sido reparado esta semana.
The bridge has been repaired this week.
The bridge will be opened tomorrow.
Las casas fueron construidas por los vecinos.
The houses were built by the neighbours.
Los resultados serán anunciados el lunes.
The results will be announced on Monday.

items.spanish: La universidad fue fundada por un grupo de estudiantes.
items.english: The university was founded by a group of students.

sections.content: The *ser* passive sounds like a news report or a history book. In conversation Spanish often prefers an active verb (*El alcalde inauguró el puente*) or the *se* passive from B1 Unit 6 (*Se inauguró el puente*). Whatever the tense, the participle agrees with the subject: *fue anunciado*, *fue anunciada*, *fueron anunciados*, *fueron anunciadas*.
